overview_markdown:
Clawith is an open-source multi-agent collaboration platform built in Python and licensed under Apache-2.0, self-described as 'OpenClaw for Teams.' Where OpenClaw focuses on a single personal assistant running locally, Clawith gives every agent a persistent identity, long-term memory, and its own workspace, then orchestrates them as a crew that collaborates with each other and with human users.

Its standout architectural feature is **Aware**, an adaptive autonomous consciousness system: agents maintain structured working memory via Focus Items with status markers, bind triggers to focus items, and proactively perceive, decide, and act instead of passively awaiting commands. Recent commits show a disciplined engineering culture — a quality tooling harness (Pyright, ESLint, Prettier baselines), an Architecture Guard, sandbox block-warning handling, and a Tool Ledger with fail-closed integrity checks for executable artifacts.

The project offers both a self-hosted open-source edition and a hosted Clawith Cloud production service, plus a shared live demo. With ~4.2k stars and frequent releases (v1.11.4-fix.1), it is actively maintained, though its community footprint outside GitHub remains thin compared to OpenClaw's massive ecosystem.
